notes: Engines door for Flight Hour Solution (Pty) Ltd. Every statement about the South African company comes from site-za/content-brief/brief.txt; nothing is taken from memory or industry knowledge. Decisions: (1) sections use the six fixed anchor ids from CONTENT-SCHEMA.md in order, each with href '#form' as the next step, so a visitor can act from any section without reading further. (2) form.id is 'form' because DoorForm renders the form element with id = form.id and the fixed hero call to action and nav anchor are '#form'; the route ('engines') and the form title still identify the form in submissions. (3) The careful wording 'through appropriately approved MROs' is kept verbatim in the shop visits section and the Execute step, with the plain statement that FHS does not overhaul or repair engines itself; FHS arranges, coordinates, sources, verifies and advises. (4) The engine type options are the Swiss site's family list, offered only as form choices, never rendered as coverage; the brief says to reuse the list only for engines the group will actually support, so it is flagged. (5) No fullScope block: the profile's section 1 to 3 lists are not in the brief, so a procurement accordion would only repeat the six sections; flagged for the client. (6) No responsePromise, no region, no figures, no years: the brief gives none. (7) Engine 360 appears only in related, with the note 'Early access'; the Monitor step says it 'is being designed', the brief's fixed wording. (8) The group's Swiss company is linked in related with the fixed country switch label 'Switzerland' and described from site/app/src/content/about.json (independent jet-engine management consultancy, Zug), labelled as the group's. (9) No image key: imagery is placed by the build agent and marked as placeholder in the hand-over note. British English, no dashes as punctuation, headlines 8 words or fewer, paragraphs 40 words or fewer, bullets 8 words or fewer.
name: Engines
seoTitle: Engine management from South Africa | Flight Hour Solution
metaDescription: Engine records, LLPs, shop visits through appropriately approved MROs, reserves, redelivery, sales and leasing. Flight Hour Solution (Pty) Ltd, South Africa.

hero.headline: Engine decisions, made on verified records
hero.sub: Records, LLPs, shop visits, reserves, redelivery, sales and leasing, for airlines, lessors, engine owners and MROs. We verify before you commit, and we sign an NDA before asking for records.

sections.title: Technical status and records
sections.text: Every engine decision starts with what the records show. We review the records and confirm the technical status before you commit to a deal, a shop visit or a return.

sections.title: LLPs and remaining life
sections.text: Remaining life on life-limited parts drives value, timing and exposure. We check the LLP stack against the records and set out what is left, before a purchase, a lease or a return.
bullets: Exposure set out before you decide

sections.title: Shop visits and MRO coordination
sections.text: We coordinate shop visits through appropriately approved MROs. We do not overhaul or repair engines ourselves. Requirement, specs and timeline are agreed first; inspections, payments and delivery are followed through.
bullets: Requirement, specs and timeline agreed first
Inspections, payments and delivery followed through

sections.title: Maintenance reserves
sections.text: Whether you pay reserves or hold them, the plan has to match the engine's real status. We help structure the maintenance plan and track exposure over the lease term.
bullets: Plan structured on status and remaining life

sections.title: Lease return and redelivery
sections.text: Redelivery is where records, status and return conditions meet. We check them against each other early and coordinate inspections through to handover, for lessee or lessor.

sections.title: Engine sales and leasing
sections.text: Buying, selling or leasing an engine. We source against your requirement, verify records and counterparties, and structure the deal through inspection, payment and delivery. Engines are quoted in US dollars.
bullets: Structured through to payment and delivery

process.title: How we work on engines
process.intro: Five steps, in this order, on every engine job.

steps.title: Define
steps.text: Your requirement, the specs and the timeline.

steps.title: Verify
steps.text: Records after an NDA, counterparties and status.

steps.title: Structure
steps.text: The deal, the lease or the maintenance plan.

steps.title: Execute
steps.text: Inspections, payments and delivery, with shop work through appropriately approved MROs.

steps.title: Monitor
steps.text: Performance and exposure after delivery. Engine 360 is being designed for this.

clientToConfirm: Engine types covered: the form offers CFM56, LEAP, V2500, PW4000, APU, TPE331 or TFE731 and Other or not sure. This is the Swiss site's family list used as choices only; nowhere on the page is it stated as coverage. Confirm which families the group will actually support for South African clients, and the options will be cut to that list.
Regions served: no region is named anywhere on the page. The form asks for region or country as free text. Confirm the regions to name once decided.
Full scope for procurement readers: the corporate profile's engine sections (1 to 3) are not in the brief, so no 'Full scope' accordion is rendered. Supply the profile's engine list to add one.
Response time: no reply time is stated on this page or under the form. Commit to one for engine enquiries, stated in SAST, only if the team can staff it.
Inbox: engines@flighthoursolution.com is a proposal. Confirm the address and who it forwards to.

Own approvals: the page says FHS coordinates shop visits through appropriately approved MROs and does not overhaul or repair engines itself. Confirm that Flight Hour Solution (Pty) Ltd holds no maintenance approval of its own; if a SACAA or other approval exists, supply it and the wording will be adjusted.

Group engineers: the Swiss company is linked in the related block, labelled as the group's. Confirm whether its engineers will work on South African engine jobs; if so, they can be named on the About page as group colleagues.

Both sides of a lease: the reserves and lease return sections address lessors and lessees alike, because the brief lists airlines, lessors and engine owners as engine visitors. Confirm FHS acts for either side.

Form choices: approve the issue options (the six sections plus Something else) and the timing options (As soon as possible, Within weeks, Within months, Planning ahead), and whether Owned or leased needs a third choice for MROs or agents acting for an owner.
Currency: the section and the form say engines are quoted in US dollars, as the brief states. Confirm.
Engine 360: the Monitor step says Engine 360 'is being designed' for performance and exposure monitoring. Confirm this description holds until launch.
